audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 fits 53.36% WR over 1964 games; a dash assassin into the anti-dash mage is the archetypal Vex-favoured lane and both layers argue it coherently.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[2] claims 'no permanent owner' while both chart layers and the packet read Vex on all 7 rows.
audit.why: Chart layers already agree; only the report sentence contradicts them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content layer fabricates mechanics: Vex W 'cleanses his slow' (W is shield+damage only, no cleanse in Riot's text), E 'fear roots his dash' (E slows and applies Gloom; the fear is the passive-empowered cast), Rake called a dash (it is a dagger volley — his dashes are Q's leap and E's vault), and a stale 'Prowler's/GA re-engage' item reference. Cooldowns field had no digits.
audit.why: Kits: Vex W 'Gain a shield and damage nearby enemies'; Talon W Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 volley, Q 8s leap outside melee, R Shadow Assault 100/80/60 invisibility, E vault putting used terrain on a long cooldown.
audit.corrected: Cleanse/root claims removed from spikes[0], whys[2], whys[3], wants.foe[0], mid; Rake-as-dash fixed in mid and spikes[3]; Prowler's replaced with Flash-GA; real cooldowns (Rake 9s, R 100s) added to breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: E-mark the contact, Q through the marked line for the fear, auto, walk — every trade he answers with a dash just schedules the next fear.
edits.after: Poke from 1200 range and hold the glow for his Q leap — the fear interrupts the dash itself, and a feared Talon has no melee crit to land.

edits.before: Spending the W pulse on poke spacing and then eating the real engage unfeared — the pulse is the matchup against everything that moves fast.
edits.after: Standing on Rake's return line — the boomerang's second pass is most of his poke, stacks Wound, and slows you for the Q leap follow-up.

edits.before: Mark and bolt — your trades are honest and your passive makes his mobility dishonest. Bank Gloom procs like currency.
edits.after: Q from 1200 range and bank the glow — before 3 his Rake poke is honest and his leap is a fear he hasn't paid for yet.

edits.before: Luden's onward, hunt the skirmishes: R into river fights, fear the convergence, and reset off whatever dies. Your range is wherever the missile reaches.
edits.after: Luden's onward, shadow his roams — Shadow Assault is 100s and his picks need it; your R snipes the rotation mid-vault and resets off the kill.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Personal Space for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and most of his lane damage — stand off the return line, step up in its downtime. - Shadow Assault is 100s: when he vanishes, W-pulse and hold the fear for the reappear. - Each wall he vaults goes on a long cooldown.

notes: Chart agrees on both layers (Vex 0-6, matching 53.36% WR) — no chart edits. Main work was killing fabricated mechanics in the content layer: Vex W described as cleansing slows (it is shield+damage only), E described as a fear/root on its own (the fear is the passive-empowered cast), Rake described as a dash (it is a thrown volley; his dashes are the Q leap and E vault), and a stale Prowler's Claw reference (item removed) swapped to Flash-GA. Real cooldowns added: Rake 9s rank 1, Shadow Assault 100s, per-terrain vault cooldown. The fear-on-dash template is genuinely apt here so the full layer needed grounding rather than reframing. dosFull[2].d / dontsFull[0].d left: short, matchup-plausible, nothing kit-false. breakdown.spikes/feeding remain templated with nothing Talon-specific to add without invention.
